era: Declaration of Internal Armed Conflict — January 2024

events.title: Los Choneros Leader 'Fito' Escapes Guayaquil Prison
events.detail: José Adolfo Macías Villamar, alias 'Fito', leader of Ecuador's largest and oldest gang Los Choneros, escapes from La Regional prison in Guayaquil hours before he is due to be transferred to a maximum-security facility. His absence is only confirmed publicly two days later. The escape, enabled by corrupt prison officials, triggers the most violent week in modern Ecuadorian history.

events.title: Noboa Declares Nationwide State of Emergency
events.detail: President Daniel Noboa, less than two months into his term, declares a 60-day nationwide state of emergency with a nightly curfew (11pm-5am) after Fito's escape triggers riots, hostage-takings by inmates, and armed attacks on public institutions across multiple provinces.

events.title: Los Lobos Leader Fabricio Colón Pico Escapes Riobamba Prison
events.detail: Fabricio Colón Pico, leader of Los Lobos — Ecuador's second-largest and fastest-growing gang, allied with the Sinaloa Cartel and Jalisco New Generation Cartel — escapes from a prison in Riobamba, compounding the crisis triggered by Fito's escape two days earlier.

events.title: Gunmen Storm TC Televisión, Take Staff Hostage on Live Air
events.detail: Armed men storm the TC Televisión studio in Guayaquil during a live broadcast, brandishing guns and explosives and taking journalists and staff hostage on camera. The images, broadcast nationally before the feed is cut, become the defining symbol of the crisis and prompt Noboa's 'internal armed conflict' declaration hours later. Police retake the station and free the hostages without loss of life.

events.title: Noboa Declares 'Internal Armed Conflict,' Names 22 Gangs Terrorist Organizations
events.detail: President Noboa signs a decree declaring Ecuador in a state of 'internal armed conflict,' formally designating 22 criminal groups — including Los Choneros and Los Lobos — as terrorist organizations and legitimate military targets. The decree authorizes the armed forces to conduct combat operations against gangs, a legal framework whose constitutionality is later questioned by Ecuador's Constitutional Court. 'We are at war, and we cannot cede in the face of these terrorist groups,' Noboa tells Canela Radio.

events.title: Prosecutor César Suárez Assassinated
events.detail: César Suárez, the prosecutor overseeing the investigation into the armed takeover of TC Televisión, is shot dead in Guayaquil in an apparent gang reprisal, underscoring the risks facing Ecuador's justice officials amid the conflict.

events.title: US Treasury Sanctions Los Choneros
events.detail: The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctions Los Choneros, freezing any US assets and barring transactions with the group as Washington begins aligning its financial enforcement tools with Ecuador's domestic terrorist designation.

events.title: Voters Approve Security Referendum
events.detail: In an 11-question referendum, Ecuadorians approve nine measures strengthening Noboa's security agenda, including allowing joint military-police street patrols (72% approval) and extraditing Ecuadorian nationals wanted abroad (65% approval), plus longer sentences for terrorism and murder. Two questions, including on legislative seat reduction, fail.

events.title: Double Car Bombing Rocks Esmeraldas
events.detail: Two car bombs explode simultaneously in the northern province of Esmeraldas — a key node on the cocaine trafficking route to Colombia already under a state of emergency — with one device detonating outside a school. The attack signals gangs' growing use of explosives as a weapon of intimidation.

events.title: US Sanctions Los Lobos and Leader 'Pipo'
events.detail: OFAC sanctions the Los Lobos Drug Trafficking Organization and its leader, Wilmer Geovanny Chavarría Barre, alias 'Pipo', blocking any US property and interests and barring US persons from dealing with them, as Los Lobos overtakes rivals to become Ecuador's largest trafficking network.

events.title: 20 Sentenced in 'Metástasis' Judicial Corruption Case
events.detail: An Ecuadorean court sentences 20 people — including Wilman Terán, former president of the National Judicial Council, and Pablo Ramírez, former head of the prisons authority SNAI — to between 40 months and 10 years for running a corruption network on behalf of drug trafficker Leandro Norero that manipulated judicial processes to favor imprisoned gang members.

events.title: 17 Killed in Guayaquil's Litoral Penitentiary Riot
events.detail: At least 15-17 inmates are killed and 14-15 injured when the 'Duendes' gang attacks rival 'Freddy Kruegers' inmates at the overcrowded Litoral Penitentiary, which holds roughly 10,000 prisoners — double its capacity. The facility, site of a 119-death massacre in 2021, remains a flashpoint despite repeated government pledges to retake control of the prison system.

events.title: Four Afro-Ecuadorian Boys Abducted by Soldiers in Las Malvinas
events.detail: Ten soldiers detain four Black boys — Steven Medina (11), Nehemías Arboleda (15), and brothers Ismael and Josué Arroyo (15 and 14) — after a soccer game in Guayaquil's Las Malvinas neighborhood, under tight military control at the time, and force them into an army truck. The boys disappear, becoming known as the 'Guayaquil Four' and the starkest emblem of alleged military abuses under Noboa's crackdown.

events.title: Charred Bodies of Missing Boys Found Near Air Force Base
events.detail: Four charred bodies are found in a marshy area of Taura, outside an Ecuadorian Air Force base, later confirmed as the remains of the four boys abducted in Las Malvinas on December 8. The discovery, on Christmas Eve, triggers national outrage and an investigation into the soldiers involved.

era: Election Year: Noboa Re-Elected, 'Fito' Recaptured — 2025 H1

events.title: Noboa, González Advance to Runoff in Security-Dominated Vote
events.detail: In Ecuador's first-round presidential election, incumbent Daniel Noboa and Revolución Ciudadana's Luisa González each win roughly 44% of the vote — separated by fewer than 20,000 ballots out of 13.8 million cast — sending the race, dominated by security concerns, to an April runoff.

events.title: Community Journalist Patricio Aguilar Murdered in Esmeraldas
events.detail: Patricio Ernesto Aguilar Vásquez, director of the community newspaper El Libertador de Quinindé, is murdered in Quinindé, Esmeraldas province, after receiving threats over his reporting on local gang violence. His killing is part of a broader surge in violence against Ecuadorian journalists, with 131 attacks recorded in 2024 alone.

events.title: Europol-Ecuador Operation Nets 73 Tons of Cocaine
events.detail: Ecuadorian and European authorities announce the dismantling of a transnational trafficking network shipping cocaine from Ecuadorian ports to Belgium, Germany, the Netherlands, and Spain, arresting 50 suspects and seizing a cumulative 73 tons of cocaine since the investigation began the previous year.

events.title: Investigation Links Noboa Family Banana Firm to Cocaine Shipments
events.detail: OCCRP and MercoPress report on Ecuadorian police documents and intercepted Balkan trafficker communications showing more than half a ton of cocaine — worth an estimated €26 million — was smuggled in banana containers exported by Noboa Trading, part of the Noboa family's Noboa Corporation, between 2020 and 2022. President Noboa's family denies knowing wrongdoing; the reporting journalist, Andrés Durán, leaves the country citing death threats.

events.title: Noboa Wins Runoff, González Alleges 'Grotesque Fraud'
events.detail: Daniel Noboa defeats Luisa González by an 11-point margin (55.6% to 44.3%) to win a first full four-year term, after deploying armed soldiers to polling stations and closing borders with Colombia and Peru on election day. González disputes the results without presenting evidence, declaring: 'I denounce, before the people, before the media and the world, that Ecuador is living under a dictatorship. This is the biggest fraud in the history of Ecuador!'

events.title: 'Fito' Recaptured in Underground Manta Bunker
events.detail: Ecuadorian security forces recapture Adolfo 'Fito' Macías at an underground bunker beneath a marble-walled house in the port city of Manta, 17 months after his prison escape triggered the conflict's declaration. He is transferred to a maximum-security prison in Guayaquil.

events.title: 'Fito' Extradited to the United States
events.detail: Macías is transferred from a maximum-security prison in Guayaquil to the airport and handed to US officials, becoming the first Ecuadorian citizen ever extradited from Ecuador to face US justice. He was indicted in Brooklyn federal court in April on seven counts of drug trafficking and gun smuggling, and pleads not guilty at arraignment.

era: FTO Designations, Prison Riots & Bombings — 2025 H2

events.title: DHS Secretary Noem Visits Ecuador
events.detail: US Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem visits Quito, meeting President Noboa and Ecuadorian security officials to expand bilateral cooperation on migration and counter-narcotics enforcement, part of a rapidly deepening US-Ecuador security relationship.

events.title: US Designates Los Choneros and Los Lobos as Foreign Terrorist Organizations
events.detail: Secretary of State Marco Rubio designates Los Choneros and Los Lobos as Foreign Terrorist Organizations and Specially Designated Global Terrorists, citing their links to the Sinaloa Cartel and Jalisco New Generation Cartel and their targeting of officials, judges, prosecutors and journalists. The designation opens the door to expanded US military and law-enforcement action against the groups.

events.title: 14 Killed in Machala Prison Riot
events.detail: Fourteen inmates are killed in clashes at a prison in Machala, El Oro province, three days before a second, deadlier riot erupts in Esmeraldas — underscoring the state's continued inability to secure Ecuador's prison system despite a new mega-prison construction program.

events.title: 17 Killed, Two Decapitated in Esmeraldas Prison Riot
events.detail: At least 17 inmates are killed, two of them decapitated, in fighting between Los Choneros- and Los Lobos-aligned prisoners at a prison in Esmeraldas near the Colombian border — the second deadly prison riot in a single week, days after 14 died in Machala.

events.title: Car Bomb Kills One Outside Guayaquil Shopping Mall
events.detail: A pickup truck packed with explosives detonates outside a shopping mall in Guayaquil, killing at least one person. Police find and controlled-detonate a second explosive-laden vehicle parked nearby. Interior Minister John Reimberg confirms the devices were found in the truck's remains.

events.title: Bridge Bombings Blamed on Local Gang and Ex-FARC Dissidents
events.detail: Explosions target two bridges in Ecuador, which officials blame on a local criminal gang acting with Colombian ex-FARC dissidents, in apparent retaliation for a major military operation against illegal mining operations tied to the groups.

events.title: El Encuentro Maximum-Security Mega-Prison Opens in Santa Elena
events.detail: The El Encuentro maximum-security prison in Santa Elena receives its first transfer of 300 inmates from the overcrowded La Roca facility in Guayaquil, part of Noboa's program — announced in January 2024 — to build new prison capacity for 12,000 inmates in an effort to break gang control over the penal system.

events.title: Alleged Los Lobos Leader Arrested in Spain
events.detail: Spanish authorities arrest a man identified as the alleged leader of Los Lobos, extending the international dragnet against Ecuador's largest trafficking organization beyond South America and underscoring the group's European cocaine distribution network.

events.title: Voters Reject Return of Foreign Military Bases
events.detail: In a four-question referendum held under a state of exception, roughly 61% of Ecuadorian voters reject lifting the constitutional ban on foreign military bases — a measure Noboa had championed to formalize the return of US forces to the Manta air base. Voters also reject ending state funding for parties, cutting the size of the National Assembly, and convening a new Constituent Assembly.

events.title: 11 Soldiers Sentenced to 34 Years for Killing 'Guayaquil Four'
events.detail: More than a year after the boys' disappearance, an Ecuadorian court finds 11 of 17 soldiers responsible for the abduction, torture, and killing of Steven Medina, Nehemías Arboleda, and the Arroyo brothers, sentencing them to the maximum 34 years and $10,000 in fines per family; five soldiers who cooperated with prosecutors receive reduced 2.5-year terms. The verdict is hailed by human rights groups as a rare instance of accountability for military abuses.

events.title: US Offers $5 Million Reward for Los Choneros Leadership
events.detail: The US State Department's Rewards for Justice program offers up to $5 million for information leading to the arrest or conviction of the current leader of the Foreign Terrorist Organization Los Choneros, as Washington escalates financial pressure on the group's post-Fito leadership.

era: Record Violence & Deepening US Military Cooperation — 2026

events.title: Noboa Declares New 60-Day State of Emergency in 9 Provinces
events.detail: President Noboa opens 2026 by declaring a fresh 60-day state of emergency across nine provinces and three municipalities, citing sustained criminal violence, as Ecuador closes out 2025 with a record national homicide rate of 50.9 per 100,000 — the highest since at least 2014.

events.title: Noboa Unveils New Security Plan After 'Most Violent Year' on Record
events.detail: Facing criticism that two years of militarized 'internal armed conflict' policy have failed to reduce violence, President Noboa announces a new security plan following what officials and analysts describe as Ecuador's most violent year in its history, with the 2025 homicide rate up 31% from 2024.

events.title: Ecuador and US Launch Joint Operations Against Designated Terrorist Groups
events.detail: Ecuadorian and US forces launch coordinated operations against Los Choneros, Los Lobos and other designated terrorist organizations, formalizing direct American operational involvement on Ecuadorian soil for the first time since the conflict began — a partnership Human Rights Watch later says was accompanied by torture, arbitrary detention, and unexplained drone strikes on fishing boats.

events.title: Ecuador Prepares Crackdown on 'Criminal Economy' with Trump Administration Backing
events.detail: Ecuador announces an expanded offensive against the financial infrastructure of trafficking organizations — money laundering, front companies, and port logistics — backed by the Trump administration, deepening bilateral security ties beyond direct kinetic operations into economic and intelligence cooperation.

events.title: UN Committee Logs 51 Enforced Disappearance Reports Since 2024
events.detail: The UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances reports it has received 51 complaints of enforced disappearance — including of children — allegedly committed by Ecuadorian law enforcement and military during security operations between 2024 and 2025, adding international scrutiny to domestic allegations of abuse under the 'internal armed conflict' framework.

events.title: Noboa Declares 60-Day Emergency Across 10 Provinces After 879 Homicides in Six Weeks
events.detail: President Noboa declares another 60-day state of emergency across 10 provinces — Guayas, Manabí, Santa Elena, Los Ríos, El Oro, Pichincha, Esmeraldas, Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas, Sucumbíos, and Azuay — suspending home inviolability after 879 homicides are recorded between May 1 and June 12, 2026, even as 2026 homicide levels ease slightly from 2025's record peak.

events.title: HRW: 'Dangerous Partnership' Report Documents US-Ecuador Operation Abuses
events.detail: Human Rights Watch publishes a 94-page report, 'A Dangerous Partnership,' documenting torture and arbitrary detention of farm workers, the burning of a dairy farm, and unexplained drone attacks on fishing boats with several fishermen missing, during joint US-Ecuador 'partnered operations.' Americas director Juanita Goebertus says: 'US-Ecuador cooperation on security has been too opaque and too dangerous for Ecuadorians,' calling for increased congressional oversight.

events.title: Noboa Orders Military Protection for Interior Minister After Assassination Plot
events.detail: President Noboa issues Executive Decree 450 ordering police and military protection for Interior Minister John Reimberg and his family, after the captured Los Tiguerones second-in-command alias 'Gato Negro' is implicated in a plot against the minister. Reimberg states: 'Alias Gato Negro also tried to attempt against my life in my capacity as Interior Minister.'

events.title: US Designates Chone Killers a Foreign Terrorist Organization
events.detail: The US State Department designated Ecuador's Chone Killers gang as a Foreign Terrorist Organization and Specially Designated Global Terrorist, effective July 2, 2026. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the group 'committed numerous attacks targeting civilians, law enforcement officers and government officials,' extending the FTO framework already applied to Los Choneros and Los Lobos in September 2025.

events.title: Argentina Designates Los Lobos, Los Choneros, Chone Killers as Terrorist Groups
events.detail: During a Quito visit by Argentine President Javier Milei on August 6, 2026, Argentina's government added the Chone Killers to its terrorism registry (RePET), following its October 2025 designation of Los Choneros and Los Lobos. Noboa and Milei signed six bilateral agreements on security, trade, and extradition; Interior Minister John Reimberg said organized crime would be pursued 'in a coordinated manner, relentlessly and with the full weight of the State.'

media.caption: Milei and Noboa meet in Quito

events.title: Noboa Extends State of Emergency 30 More Days Across 10 Provinces
events.detail: President Daniel Noboa signed Executive Decree 472 on August 14, 2026, extending the state of exception first declared June 17 for another 30 days across Guayas, Manabí, Santa Elena, Los Ríos, El Oro, Pichincha, Esmeraldas, Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas, Sucumbíos, and Azuay provinces plus the cantons La Maná, Las Naves, and La Troncal. The decree cites 238,404 emergency calls logged between July 1 and August 5, 2026, of which 68.3% related to citizen security, and keeps suspended the inviolability of the home and of correspondence.

media.caption: Noboa renews the state of exception

events.title: Three Minors Killed in Guayaquil Home Invasion
events.detail: Around six armed men on two motorcycles forced their way into a home in the Flor de Bastión sector of Guayaquil's Nueva Prosperina district on the night of August 14, 2026, and opened fire, killing a 7-year-old and two teenagers aged 13 and 15. The children's father was shot and hospitalized; investigators recovered 18 shell casings and are probing a possible link to the Los Tiguerones gang or a case of mistaken identity, as the family reported no prior threats.

media.caption: Investigators at the scene in Nueva Prosperina

events.title: Four Killed in Los Choneros–Los Lobos Clash in Babahoyo
events.detail: Gunmen raided two homes in the La Margarita sector of Pimocha parish, Babahoyo canton, Los Ríos province, before dawn on August 16, 2026, killing four people — three men and a 17-year-old — believed to belong to Los Lobos. Police said the attack, attributed to Los Choneros, was retaliation for the theft of a motorcycle belonging to a Los Choneros member; a fifth victim, a woman, was wounded.

media.caption: Scene of the Babahoyo gang clash

events.title: US Treasury Sanctions 15 Targets, 10 Vessels in Manta-Based Cocaine Network
events.detail: OFAC designated 15 individuals and companies plus 10 fishing vessels on August 20, 2026, in a network operating from Manta that allegedly used fishing boats as cover to refuel and resupply 'go-fast' boats moving thousands of kilograms of cocaine monthly toward Mexico, where the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG took over distribution to the United States. The network is affiliated with FTOs Los Choneros and Los Lobos. Defense Minister Gian Carlo Loffredo said Ecuador would 'triple maritime interdiction capabilities' in the affected zone.

events.title: Prosecutor Investigating Organized Crime — Later Linked to Drone-Strike Probe — Assassinated in Manta
events.detail: Manabí prosecutor Gloria Alexandra Bravo Cedeño, 46, was shot dead by a motorcycle gunman near midday on June 14, 2026, at the intersection of Flavio Reyes Avenue and Calle 22 in central Manta; her sister Olinda Emperatriz Bravo Cedeño was killed trying to shield her, and a bystander was wounded. Bravo Cedeño, with over 15 years as a prosecutor in Manabí, was handling homicide, kidnapping, and organized-crime cases, including a June 6, 2026 investigation into the burning of 27 vessels in Manta; Ecuador's Fiscalía attributed the killing to retaliation for that organized-crime casework and noted she is the third prosecutor assassinated in Manta since 2022. She had reportedly warned for months she was at risk and normally moved under police escort, which was absent at the time of the attack. Separately, unconfirmed reporting from July and August 2026 has linked her death to an earlier investigation she opened into alleged US drone strikes on Ecuadorian fishing boats near the Galápagos — a connection Ecuadorian authorities have not officially confirmed and that mainstream outlets covering the later CIA revelations did not make.

media.caption: Aftermath of the attack on Flavio Reyes Avenue, Manta

events.confidenceReason: The assassination itself is confirmed by multiple Tier 1-2 Ecuadorian outlets and HRW; the alleged link to the drone-strike investigation rests on Tier 4 alternative-media reporting not corroborated by Ecuadorian authorities or the mainstream outlets that broke the CIA story.

events.title: Investigations Link Covert US Program to Drone Strikes on Ecuadorian Fishing Boats
events.detail: New York Times (Aug 12, 2026) and Washington Post (Aug 13, 2026) investigations reported that at least three Ecuadorian fishing vessels were attacked in Ecuador's exclusive economic zone near the Galápagos in early 2026: the Fiorella disappeared with 8 of its crew on January 20, 2026 and remains missing, presumed dead per the UN; the Negra Francisca Duarte II (16 crew) was drone-bombed and set ablaze on March 17, 2026; and the Don Maca (20 crew) was struck on March 26, 2026. Survivors on the latter two vessels said armed, English-speaking men in matching uniforms with US flag patches operating from an unmarked 'ghost ship' hooded and detained them at sea for days before handing them to the Salvadoran Navy as shipwreck victims. The Washington Post reported an unregistered aircraft tied to US defense contractor Shield AI was detected roughly 500 meters from the Negra Francisca hours after the March 17 attack, and that the aircraft was registered through a shell company using a UPS store mailbox in Richmond, Virginia; an anonymous source described the operation as a covert CIA action requiring presidential authorization. The US Coast Guard and Pentagon denied any involvement, and a CIA spokesperson told CNN it had 'no guidance to offer.' Ecuadorian legal counsel Jorge Chiriboga Dávalos said: 'You cannot attack civilian vessels. That is an abuse and that is what we reject.'

media.caption: Fishermen carry their catch at Playita Mía in Manta

events.confidenceReason: US Coast Guard, Pentagon, and CIA have denied or declined to confirm involvement; NYT/WaPo reporting relies on survivor testimony, aircraft registration records, and an anonymous source describing a covert-action program, none of which Ecuadorian or US authorities have officially confirmed.

events.title: US Deploys Warships, Black Hawks, and Special Forces to Ecuador Under 'Shield of the Americas'
events.detail: Esmeraldas Governor Juan Jaramillo confirmed at an August 18, 2026 press conference that the US and Ecuadorian governments are jointly operating against narcoterrorism in San Lorenzo, Río Verde, and Eloy Alfaro cantons, with reporting identifying US Army 7th Special Forces Group personnel working alongside Ecuadorian troops — the first public confirmation of a relationship SOUTHCOM and Ecuador had described since March 2026. On August 20, 2026, Defense Minister Gian Carlo Loffredo announced the arrival at Manta of two US Navy warships with interceptor boats and three UH-60 Black Hawk helicopters, following a visit from SOUTHCOM commander Gen. Francis Donovan; Loffredo said the assets would be 'positioned in the drug trafficking route, between the continental part and Galápagos' and would triple Ecuador's maritime interdiction capacity. The deployment follows a ministerial agreement published in Ecuador's Official Registry granting SOFA immunity and visa-free status for up to 180 days to US military personnel, Defense Department civilians, and contractors, building on Noboa's June 2026 decree authorizing allied foreign forces to deploy in the hardest-hit provinces. The buildup is part of the US-led 'Shield of the Americas' / Western Hemisphere Joint Task Force framework spanning roughly 18 regional partners.

media.caption: Black Hawk helicopters positioned for anti-trafficking operations

events.confidenceReason: Confirmed on record by Ecuador's Defense Minister and Esmeraldas governor, corroborated by multiple outlets.

events.title: Police Seize 1.01 Tons of Cocaine Hidden in Machinery at Posorja Port
events.detail: Ecuador's National Police, in coordination with the Fiscalía, executed Operation Fénix-0438 'Encuentro 117' at the Posorja deep-water port on August 21, 2026, seizing 1.01 tonnes (1,011.52 kg) of cocaine distributed across 928 blocks hidden inside the structures of four pieces of machinery loaded in a container declared as an 'electromagnetic lifting system' bound for the port of Lázaro Cárdenas, Mexico. The container had been flagged as high-risk on August 13 by CIAPA, the joint port/airport risk-analysis center, and was opened for inspection on August 20 under prosecutorial authorization. The Interior Ministry estimated the load's street value at roughly $2.1 million in Ecuador, $27.7 million in the US, and $43.17 million in Europe — about 9.23 million individual doses.
